text: You just filmed a screen and it's crawling with rainbow waves.
Up close that screen is a grid of tiny glowing dots.
Your camera has its own grid of tiny squares that catch light.
Lay one grid over the other just a bit off and they drift in and out of line.
Where they line up it's bright and where they don't it's dark.
Each square only sees red or green or blue so the stripes turn rainbow.
Then come the dark bars because lots of screens flash on and off hundreds of times a second.
Your camera reads one row at a time so some rows catch the screen off.
Tilt your phone or step back and the waves fade.
And that's why screens look weird on camera. Send this to someone who films their TV and subscribe.
